svg.aria-label: How a Leverage Short works. 1,000 USDC of equity goes into the Collateral Vault, which mints 1,000 USDCn. The short market lends 3,000 of AAPLr. The AAPLr is sold to the Receiver Pool for 3,000 USDCn. All 4,000 USDCn is posted on the short market as collateral for the loan, all in one transaction. You end with 4,000 USDCn posted and a 3,000 AAPLr loan: a 3x short. Your loan-to-value starts at 75 percent and you are liquidated at Null's 96.5 percent LLTV: a price rise of about 29 percent. You pay the short borrow rate, while your USDCn collateral keeps earning interest.
svg.title: How a Leverage Short works
